Current administrative boundary of each National Forest (not the roads/trails MVUM layer). Fetched once and cached for the session.

        Source: USDA Forest Service EDW
      


      
      

      

        
Color-coded by land-managing agency — nationwide BLM Surface Management Agency data.

        

          

            BLM
            USFS
            NPS
            FWS
            BOR
            Tribal
            DOD
            State
            Local
          

        

        Source: BLM Surface Management Agency
      


      

        
        
      

      


      
      
Loading forest closures…

      

      

        
Current standing forest orders on National Forest land in OR, WA, AZ, NM, ID, NV & UT — fire restrictions/closures, firearm restrictions, motor vehicle prohibitions, recreation closures, and more. Fire-related closures show as a red crosshatch; every other order type shows as a calmer solid fill. Tap any closure for details and a link to the real signed order. Fetched once and cached for the session.

        

          

            Fire-related
            Other orders
          

        

        

        Source: USDA Forest Service (Regions 3, 4 & 6)
      


      
      

      

        
      

      

        
Real USFS Motor Vehicle Use Map roads and trails, shown in the official MVUM colors — black solid = open to all vehicles, gray = seasonal restriction, dashed = special designation or narrow trail. Pick a vehicle type above to highlight matching routes with a gold outline; everything else stays visible, just dimmed — nothing is ever hidden. Tap any route for full vehicle-type and seasonal-date detail. Zoom in to load data for the visible area.

        

          

            Open to all
            Highway-legal only
            Seasonal
            Highlighted match
          

        

        

        Source: USDA Forest Service EDW
      

    

  


  

    
    

      
      

      

        
NOAA daily snow depth analysis, updated ~4x/day. Image overlay from a live federal server; shows no data in snow-free areas (correct behavior).

        Source: NOAA NOHRSC
      


      
      

      

      
Modeled air quality, not a live reading — NOAA's bias-corrected PM2.5 forecast guidance, refreshed ~2x/day. A fire that started in the last several hours won't be reflected yet. Viewing this from a downloaded offline area shows data as of download time — it won't update again until you're back online or re-download.

      

        
Near-surface PM2.5 concentration — the standard basis for wildfire-smoke air quality — colored on the real, standard EPA AQI scale (green/yellow/orange/red/purple/maroon), using NOAA's bias-corrected guidance (calibrated against real ground-station readings for better accuracy). Same live-image-overlay architecture as Snow Depth above.

        Source: NOAA / NWS Air Quality
      


      
      

      

      

        
Total smoke through the full atmospheric column, not just ground level — useful for spotting smoke aloft that hasn't reached the surface yet. This is a different measurement than the AQI layer above (total smoke mass, not a health-based air-quality value), which is why its own color scale looks different — there's no standard AQI-style palette for column smoke. Same modeled/twice-daily-refresh caveat as the AQI layer above.

        Source: NOAA / NWS Air Quality
      


      
      

      

        
USGS Annual National Land Cover Database, 2025 — habitat types across the contiguous US.

        

          

            Forest
            Shrubland
            Grass
            Water
            Developed
          

        

        Source: USGS MRLC NLCD
      


      
      

      

        
Current/active wildland fire perimeters — re-fetched live each time this layer is turned on. Contained and stale small fires are dropped by the source service automatically.

        Source: NIFC WFIGS
      


      
Disturbance History


      
      


      
      


      
      

      
      

        
      

      

        
Historical wildland fire perimeters, split into 3 independently-toggleable time ranges — turn on only the ones you need to keep loading fast. Each range has its own internal recency-gradient (freshest in light yellow-orange, oldest in deep red/maroon). Any combination can be active at once; a fire only ever falls in one range. Re-queried live as you pan and zoom.

        

          
Recent (0-20 yrs)

          

            <1 yr
            1-5 yrs
            5-10 yrs
            10-20 yrs
          

          
Older (20-50 yrs)

          

            20-30 yrs
            30-40 yrs
            40-50 yrs
          

          
Even Older (50+ yrs)

          

            50-75 yrs
            75-100 yrs
            100+ yrs
          

        

        Source: NIFC Interagency Fire Perimeter History
      


      
      

      

        
Reported timber harvest activity from the last 15 years. Tap an area for its completion year.

        

        Source: USDA Forest Service EDW (FACTS)
      


      
      

      

        
Reported timber stand improvement / thinning activity from the last 15 years. Tap an area for its completion year.

        

        Source: USDA Forest Service EDW (FACTS)
      


      
      

      

        
Per-pixel slope steepness, color-banded starting at 20° — terrain gentler than that isn't shaded. Color key shown on the map itself while this layer is on.

        
Computed on your device from the same elevation data as Elevation (DEM), in a background thread — no extra download, and it stops rendering past the same max zoom DEM itself has.

      


      
      
      

        
        
        
        
      

      

      

        
Which way each slope faces, color-mapped by temperature: blue (north) is coldest, green-yellow (east) gets morning sun, orange-red (south) is warmest, purple (west) gets afternoon heat. Flat ground isn't shaded.

        

          

            

              N
              E
              S
              W
            

          

        

        
The 4 N/E/S/W checkboxes show just the directions you pick; the main checkbox is a master switch that hides/shows your picks without losing them. Can't be on with Slope Angle at once. Computed on-device, in the background — no extra download.

      


      
      

        

          
          
        

        

          
          
        

        

      

      

        
Highlights terrain within the min/max elevation band you set — a blank tool with no built-in presets, for whatever range matters to you right now.

        
Computed on your device from the same elevation data as Elevation (DEM), in a background thread — no extra download. Min/max and opacity are remembered, but this layer's on/off state isn't — it's meant for one task at a time, so it always starts off when you reopen the app.

      

    

  


  

    
    

      
      

        
USGS rivers, streams & lakes from the National Hydrography Dataset (NHDPlus HR) — live queried for the visible map area, zoom in past Z10 to load. Tap a river, stream, or lake to see its name.

        
Reflects recently browsed areas — not included in offline downloads.

        Source: USGS NHD
      


      
      

        
USGS stream gauge stations — live queried for the visible map area, zoom in past Z8 to load. Tap a station for its most recent streamflow, gage height, and water temperature readings.

        
Reflects recently browsed areas — not included in offline downloads.

        Source: USGS Water Data

Base layers

    


    
Additional data

    

    
Active fire perimeters can't be downloaded — that data goes stale fast and could be dangerous if shown out of date offline. Hydrography and stream gauges aren't included either (live queries only — you'll only see what you've recently browsed). Wildfire History, Timber, and AQI smoke DO download and work offline, but as a snapshot frozen at download time.
